📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Russell Brand issued a statement from prison, insisting he is “not guilty” after being sentenced to 10 years and six months behind bars for rape and sexual assault.

It has been revealed that “Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening,” the comedian, 51, said in a statement shared by his wife, Laura Brand, via his YouTube channel on Sunday, November 15.

According to recent reports, laura, 39, had begun the video by stating that “Russell has asked me to read something to you today” before turning to a notebook to share her husband’s message. The post served as the first time Laura has publicly addressed Russell’s conviction and prison sentence, which was delivered in London’s Southwark Crown Court on Monday, November 9.

Russell’s message continued, “The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do. I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey. Little as in small, and hey as in, ‘Hey, I’m in the biggest sex offenders prison in Europe.’ The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind and they are dedicated. And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone.”.

Russell went to trial for four weeks, ultimately being found guilty by a jury on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Russell had repeatedly denied accusations of wrongdoing, and was found not guilty on two other rape charges and an attempted indecent assault charge.

Industry observers note that laura, who shares three children with Russell, concluded on behalf of her husband, “I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me. Let us all love, pray for and forgive one another as God forgave us. Please support my treasured wife and family. I feel your prayers. Your brother in Christ, Russell.”.

According to recent reports, since receiving his conviction and sentencing, Russell has been accused of misconduct by six additional women. London’s Metropolitan Police later confirmed to Us that he remains under investigation for additional rape allegations from two unidentified women.

A Met spokesperson told Us, “The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations. Files have been submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service in relation to both complainants. Detectives remain in close contact with prosecutors as enquiries continue and further investigative work is carried out.”.

Industry observers note that “Obviously, [it] will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my companion and my person with me,” she told fans. “Although Russell is not here now in this moment, the Holy Spirit is moving, and the Holy Spirit cannot be restrained. I’m speaking to Russell. He’s OK and he’s praying, unsurprisingly. He’s praying, and we decided for me to continue.”.

Three Ways to Avoid CAPTCHA Prompts When Using a VPN

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, VPNs make it harder to track your online activity across websites, but it also makes them suspicious about your origins.
  • That mentioned, you don’t have to keep clicking on those traffic lights over and over.
  • According to recent reports, CAPTCHAs are simple puzzles that websites use to filter out bots and spam.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, VPNs make it harder to track your online activity across websites, but it also makes them suspicious about your origins. When you borrow an IP address that hundreds of other people are also using for any number of reasons, you’re much more likely to get repeat verification requests from online firewalls.

That mentioned, you don’t have to keep clicking on those traffic lights over and over. You can simply switch to a more reputable VPN server. Moreover, browsers now offer persistent access tokens to eliminate CAPTCHA requests, while VPNs offer dedicated IPs to keep sites from getting suspicious. Here are three easy fixes for repeat CAPTCHA prompts when using a VPN, so you don’t have to trade convenience for online privacy.

According to recent reports, CAPTCHAs are simple puzzles that websites use to filter out bots and spam. They’re supposed to be easy for people but hard for robots, such as simple object recognition tasks or audio-visual challenges. However, they can still disrupt your browsing experience if they happen too frequently.

In a recent development, most modern CAPTCHA providers, like Google's reCAPTCHA v3 or Cloudflare Turnstile, start working long before they give you a puzzle to solve. It usually starts with a risk score that studies your IP address, browser and device signals, or recent online activity.

According to recent reports, if the CAPTCHA provider can’t confidently identify your request as human based on those signals, it requests that you complete a puzzle before deciding if the request should be blocked. That means when you get repeat CAPTCHA requests, there’s something affecting your browser’s risk score. For example, popular VPN servers spread the same IP address across any number of customers, which can easily make a website mistake you for a bot farm. If you change your IP address frequently by switching servers often, that might look suspicious too.

According to recent reports, luckily, there are ways to deal with frequent CAPTCHA requests using tools and services available with your browser and VPN. Cloudflare has already cut its CAPTCHA requests by 91% using its Managed Challenge platform. Apple has also been shipping token-based verification on devices since iOS 16 and macOS Ventura. In June 2026, Cloudflare even announced a joint effort called the Private Access Control Tokens (PACT) standard with Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Shopify.

While there’s no direct off switch for CAPTCHAs, you can use different fixes to improve your browser’s trust signals when using the internet. That way, you’re less likely to be hounded by verification requests.

The easiest fix for repeat CAPTCHAs is to stop connecting to whichever server your VPN app picks automatically. Proton recommends choosing servers with lower traffic load. In fact, its apps display load as a percentage to help you avoid the most crowded options. I'd also skip significant traffic hubs like Fresh York or London, since that's where most traffic originates from. Servers in smaller cities located nearby are often just as fast but never as populated.

You should also avoid changing IP addresses too frequently, which can look suspicious on its own. Pick a server that seems to behave well, then continue using it for at least one session. Also remember you’re more likely to get premium server options if you’re on a paid VPN plan. Major platforms like ExpressVPN, Surfshark, Proton, and Nord are particularly likely to have a larger server collection to pick from.

Costs nothing more than your current subscription.

Easy to switch to a different location.

Server reputations shift over time.

Hopping between servers often can backfire.

Free intends limit server options.

It has been revealed that private Access Tokens (PAT) let you verify the authenticity of your request using your device rather than an IP address. Apple calls it Automatic Verification, where an Apple server validates your device and Apple Account to assign you an anonymous token.

Industry observers note that to enable Automatic Verification on an iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification. On a Mac, open System Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, there’s no equivalent feature for Windows, Android, and Linux people. That said, Cloudflare offers the Silk extension for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge that serves a similar function. A quick look at the ratings will tell you it’s not as effective, but Cloudflare’s upcoming cross-browser standard called PACT seems promising once it is released.

Enabled by default on Apple devices.

Doesn't depend on your VPN or IP address.

Doesn’t share personal details with websites.

Native support for Apple devices only.

Not every site requests privacy tokens.

Chrome and Firefox extensions can be unreliable.

Recent findings suggest that if you pay a bit extra for a dedicated IP add-on, VPN providers can assign you a unique IP address that isn’t shared with anyone else. For example, NordVPN offers dedicated IPs in 30 countries for $2-5 a month and Surfshark charges $3.75 a month for it.

There are also dedicated providers like Private Internet Access, which charges $3.99 per month for a zero-trust setup so not even their employees know which IP address is assigned to you. On the other hand, Proton VPN offers dedicated IPs only to business blueprint users, so you’ll need to be on the Workspace Standard, Premium, or Enterprise intends to get one.

That noted, there is a trade-off here too. NordVPN itself admits that a dedicated IP makes it easier to link online activity back to a single user. Also, many websites can still tell that the IP address originated from a VPN data center rather than a consumer’s device.

Get unique IP addresses with pristine reputation.

Works across desktop, mobile, and even smart TVs.

Also functions as an allowlisted address for work.

Add-ons cost more on top of the VPN subscription.

Offers less anonymity than shared VPN servers.

Locations are locked in once you pay.

The Witcher 3 uses gen-AI to enhance Geralt's Polish voice following actor's stroke - "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
  • Recent findings suggest that the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a company called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.

Recent findings suggest that the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.

Recent findings suggest that it's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a company called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology. As confirmed to Game File, an AI trained on Rozenek's previous Witcher work is retreating his recordings to make them sound more like the Geralt you hear elsewhere in The Witcher 3.

"The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust ... for the creators of this game.".

In a recent development, game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

This isn't the first time CD Projekt Red has used generative AI for voice recordings in one of its games. The studio worked with Respeecher in 2023 to produce new voiceover lines for Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty. Viktor Vektor actor Miłogost "Miłek" Reczek passed away in 2021, after the original game was released, and CD Projekt Red didn't want to recast the role. Reczek's sons apparently gave their blessing for their father's voice to be artificially generated.

"I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically with consent and also to do something good," CD Projekt Red localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File, referring to the Rozenek recordings.

Industry observers note that "For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all. It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that there is this difference.".

In a recent development, the third Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, releases at some point next year, an unprecedented 12 years after the original game debuted. It adds an entirely new region, Letten, and centres its main story around Geralt's missing bardic bestie Dandelion, whose family lives there.

It has been revealed that in preparation for the expansion, a remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released a couple of months ago, overhauling the old role-playing adventure and bringing its baseline presentation more in line with what we'd expect from a modern game; it also overhauled some animations and enemy behaviours and reworked skill trees. For that reason, old-gen consoles PS4 and Xbox One won't receive the Songs of the Past expansion, despite The Witcher 3 being available on them.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that I decided to hop into the beta branch myself and take her for a whirl, and—yeah, those changes'll have to come.
  • This is a little busted, because by default, the Fool has 6 aim already put in her bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Slay the Spire 2 has a new character—notably, a new character in testing—and as the patch notes themselves point out, that testing will very much be needed: "We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch.".

Industry observers note that I decided to hop into the beta branch myself and take her for a whirl, and—yeah, those changes'll have to come. The Fool's central mechanic is her bow and arrow—she can fire an arrow/shoot card to deal damage equal to the card's base damage plus her aim. So if a shoot card deals 15 damage and she has six aim stocked, she'll deal 21.

This is a little busted, because by default, the Fool has 6 aim already put in her bank. Her non-strike starter card, Foolish Shot, already deals a hefty 15 damage for just one energy. With aim, the first time she uses it, it deals a whopping 21 damage, which is a heck of a damage output for the Fool's first round of combat.

Recent findings suggest that the saving grace here is that when a card that fires an arrow is used, that arrow becomes lodged in a target, who gains the Impale status. You can't play any more arrow-based cards until you either Dislodge (another game term, hence the proper nounage) an arrow with a card that dislodges, or until you have more than one arrow.

Recent findings suggest that in my runs, I wasn't able to figure out the latter. But I really didn't need to, because I was one-shotting bosses the whole way up the spire. One card in particular, Repeat Shot, seems borderline broken. While it is a rare, it shoots a target for 20 damage (when upgraded) X times, plus your current aim.

With precious little setup, I was casually knocking (or should I say nocking) out around 78 damage on turn one just by having the card pop into my hand. Add even a little aim generation to your deck, and Repeat Shot solves single-target fights for you. By making them dead.

There are some other interesting mechanics, too, such as a trio of melodies you can activate and trigger other cards off of. Wah Blast, for instance, hits twice if you've got a Cho or Ki melody active. There's also Stretch, which gives you extra block on the usage of your next block card, Sadness, a status card that can be turned into Joy which gives you energy and card draw, and tarot cards via a power called Mythic Form.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Obviously, she's broken. I absolutely shouldn't be one-card tapping bosses on Act 1 just because I happened to first-turn draw into a single rare card. But she is already very fun, and I look forward to seeing what more balanced version of The Fool will look like in the full game.

According to recent reports, other than that, the testing branch now has two fresh modes: Blitz, a more bite-sized version where there's no map or gold, and Dread, which appears to be an Ascension+ mode for masochists. Could never be me.

Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.

After days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has announced Huang's resignation as manufacturer president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately. Finance chief Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO and will remain in the position until a permanent CEO is chosen.

Sources indicate that "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news. "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.".

Kress, in the same announcement, indicates she intends to build on the foundation laid by Huang over the past 33 years, and "continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Perhaps unsurprisingly, there's no mention of gaming graphics cards in there.

Industry observers note that nvidia's announcement ends by thanking Huang for his time at the company: "Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.".

Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang amid allegations he had participated in a second affair, this time with a subordinate, following reports of his alleged affair with a Chinese spy. That initial incident prompted a organization-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation exploring whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Nvidia will likely remain under increased scrutiny moving forward. There are particular concerns around the company's chips being imported to China despite trade bans.

Sources indicate that “I was excommunicated from the LDS church right about the time I was either pregnant with Logan or had just had Logan,” Janelle, 57, revealed during the Sunday, November 15, episode of the TLC series. (Janelle and Kody, 57, share six children: Logan, 32, Maddie, 31, Hunter, 29, Gabe, 25, Savanah, 21, and son Garrison, who died in March 2024 at the age of 25.).

She recalled that after marrying Kody in 1993 and becoming his second wife, the LDS church, which she was raised in, shunned her.

“I was, like, 24 and I remember the letter coming to our house,” Janelle shared. “Kody was not involved. It was just me. Yeah, they excommunicated me.”.

Industry observers note that the LDS church practices mainstream Mormonism. Kody and his wives initially practiced Mormon fundamentalism, and were specifically part of the Apostolic United Brethren (AUB), before they all slowly distanced themselves from the religion.

Janelle, for her part, revealed on Sunday’s episode that she still has a “spiritual life” but it’s not under a specific umbrella.

According to recent reports, “I have a relationship with God. I just don’t have a church I worship with,” she shared. “I’m kind of waiting for some sign that I need to go somewhere or I belong somewhere. I don’t know.”.

Janelle also noted that during her first marriage to ex-sister wife Meri Brown’s brother, she actually had her husband join the LDS church.

However, once that marriage ended, Janelle remained close with Meri’s family, who were polygamists, and that sparked her own interest in the practice.

It has been revealed that “I felt a spiritual calling. I made this decision. It wasn’t because I was — I thought I was less than. I didn’t think it was because I only deserved this,” Janelle told former sister wife and close friend Christine Brown. “I chose it because I felt like it was a calling and it wasn’t anything to do with my perception of what I was worth or what I was entitled to or what I deserved.”.

Christine, 54, pointed out, “You found the value in it. I think we were talking about this the other day, that there was value because you were believing in a community.”.

Janelle agreed, adding, “I thought that we would have some sort of really great communal family experience or something.”.

While all of Kody’s now-ex wives initially bought into the polygamist lifestyle, three of his wives have walked away in recent years.

Industry observers note that christine announced her split from Kody in 2021 after more than 25 years of a spiritual marriage. Janelle revealed in December 2022 that she and Kody had been separated for months.

#4454. Beto O’Rourke States He’d “Do Anything” for James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa—Including Work for Them

Beto O’Rourke States He’d “Do Anything” for James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa—Including Work for Them

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, “Should I have talked to Joe Hagan when he was on my front porch in 2019?” O’Rourke claims now, looking back at the cover story I wrote, in which he proclaimed he was “just born to be in it,” a premature declaration that almost immediately sank his prospects.
  • O'Rourke taks the stage during the Fight the Trump Takeover rally at the Texas Capitol in August 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that after the shocking Democratic victories in Texas last week, it was hard not to look over the shoulders of James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa and see the shadow of Beto O’Rourke, whose losses for Senate in 2018 and governor in 2022 had become cautionary tales of Democratic hopelessness in Texas. And perhaps proof that nice guys couldn’t win. But in the years after those failed runs, O’Rourke never really went away. He rolled out a voter-registration group called Powered by People, punched out missives on Substack, livestreamed his thoughts, and quietly advised his party from the background.

In a recent development, “Should I have talked to Joe Hagan when he was on my front porch in 2019?” O’Rourke claims now, looking back at the cover story I wrote, in which he proclaimed he was “just born to be in it,” a premature declaration that almost immediately sank his prospects. “I’m glad I did. I’m grateful for everything that’s happened, because look where we are. It’s a beautiful new day in America.”.

O'Rourke taks the stage during the Fight the Trump Takeover rally at the Texas Capitol in August 2025.

Like Stacey Abrams in Georgia, who lost her own race for governor but used her visibility to build a stronger coalition, O’Rourke can claim some credit for setting the table for Democratic success in Texas. Talarico won his first race, for a Republican-held state House seat, on O’Rourke’s 2018 wave. And as it turns out, O’Rourke himself weighed another Senate run this year. When Talarico asked whether he’d run, O’Rourke mentioned only if Talarico ran for governor instead, eventually stepping aside after concluding that the moment called for “something and someone new.” When he released his Senate campaign, Talarico said he wanted to replicate O’Rourke’s “energy.”.

According to recent reports, O’Rourke, meanwhile, became a behind-the-scenes player: Powered by People was one of four partners in the Texas Democrats’ $30 million coordinated campaign, and it says it reached more than 110,000 newly introduced and young voters in Texas this cycle. Ken Paxton noticed and tried to put O’Rourke “behind bars” for funding the Democrats who fled the state to block its Donald Trump–backed redistricting.

O’Rourke states the wave cascaded so far down the ballot in Texas that a candidate who tried backing out of her campaign before Election Day ended up winning. “At that point it was too late to take her name off the ballot,” he says. “She didn’t campaign, just won her election. That speaks to the magnitude of the wave, but also to the value of having a fighter on every front. Somebody said to me, ‘A wave’s great, even better if you have a surfboard.’”.

Over an hour-long conversation, O’Rourke parses the political revolution in his home state, suggests how Democrats can hold on to their land grab, and, perhaps unsurprisingly, looks ahead to another run for office.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Vanity Fair: The conventional wisdom is that this was a revolt against Trump, and that the candidates and the Democratic strategy were secondary. What’s your read?

It has been revealed that beto O’Rourke: So much of this election was a rejection of Trump and Trumpism: the corruption, the wars, the cruelty. But after 2024, people were anxious that we didn’t have a unifying national leader. [Joe] Biden was not going to be it. Kamala Harris turned out not to be it. President Obama, I think wisely, held back…. Chuck Schumer was persona non grata in any gathering of Democrats. The DNC was in the red.

What it did was allow for candidates in different parts of the country to really establish themselves in their own right and by their own merits, never having to fear being under the shadow of a larger figure. It’s really a blessing. That’s how you get Abdul El-Sayed, James Talarico, Mary Peltola, all these extraordinary candidates who are extraordinarily different from each other. In Texas, for the first time in half a century, Democrats fielded a fighter on every front: 150 state House candidates, 38 congressional candidates, 16 state Senate candidates. You had to have a historically terrible, corrupt president. But you also had to have this historically beaten-down Democratic Party; that the Democrats don’t have a message, they don’t have a leader. That all turned out to be a great thing.

It has been revealed that A year ago you convened Talarico, Colin Allred, and Joaquin Castro to think about a statewide slate. Talarico went his own way. You warned him he’d “want friends on that ticket.” What did you mean?

According to recent reports, I just wanted to win, and I put that before anything else. James and I had many conversations before he officially revealed. He asked me, “Are you interested? Would you run?” And I told him, “The only condition on which I would run is if you were to run for governor, or somebody else who could draw that kind of attention and resources, and if we had the ticket rounded out by strong contenders for every position on the ballot.”.

My advice to him was: “Look, I’ve done this before. No matter how talented you are, no matter how much you can raise, this state is so significant, the Republicans are so entrenched, you need a fighter on every front.” And ultimately, that’s what happened. Gina really hit her stride at the right time. Her strength as a candidate a year ago compared to how she finished is worlds apart, and that is a testament to what an exceptional leader she is.

Clearly, it was the right call for James to be there. He is just an extraordinarily talented communicator. He was a phenomenally focused candidate. He was absolutely the right guy for the moment. I also think it was the right call for Jasmine Crockett to run too. I know from being on college campuses how electrifying she is, how many young people she brought into the electorate this time. They stayed in even after Jasmine was defeated in the primary.

In a recent development, the Atlantic reported that you told Hinojosa, “Not one person can win Texas. It has to be two.” Is that what you said?

I definitely spoke to Gina before she made the decision to run, and then after. To be honest with you, I can’t remember if I said “two.” What I said consistently to everybody who was thinking about it—Colin, Joaquin, Gina, Jasmine [Crockett], James—was that you need a fighter on every front and the strongest possible ticket. That was based on the last run I had, in 2022, and even the ’18 run. If Joaquin or Julián Castro had run for governor when I was running for Senate, who knows? Of course, at that time, we didn’t know the size of the wave that was about to crash.

It has been revealed that I definitely did. I could have run…. You’d have to ask James, but I think he probably would have supported that if I had. We have an amazing organization in waiting, volunteers who’ve been with me, the ability to raise money. But was that the right thing to do? No. I had been before Texas twice before, and the moment demanded something different and, I would argue, something better.

Industry observers note that you can’t discount a politician’s ambition and ego. I had to find a way to get past that. It helped having conversations with my wife. It helped having conversations with our kids. It helped having conversations with people who’d been on these runs with me before. Also, I spent a lot of time traveling Texas. My love language is a town hall meeting, where it’s just a free-for-all and anybody can step to the mic and ask any questions. At the end of that, I really felt this moment called for something and someone new. I don’t know that Texas could have produced a stronger—I was going to say candidate, but really a one-two punch. It was James and Gina. They’re both exceptional individually. Together, they transcended what had happened in politics for as long as I’ve been alive.

Industry observers note that honestly, my own doubt about whether Texas could be won was based on you. We’d seen this story before.

In a recent development, I wouldn’t have done this work as a volunteer for the last four years if I didn’t believe in Texas. I know in my heart and in my bones that we are so much better than the people in power. It’s the obscene abortion ban that has cost the lives of girls and women, the $7.25-an-hour minimum wage, the fact that we’re the least insured state in the country. Four years after Uvalde, and no one in power has done a single thing. It’s insane having Texas Republicans say, if you’re Muslim, regardless of whether you’re an immigrant, you should be deported from this country. That’s just not who we are.

O'Rourke speaks during the Fight the Trump Takeover rally, where 5,000 people attended. Attendees protested proposed redistricting, immigration enforcement, and other Trump-backed legislation and proposed changes.

According to recent reports, when I ran for governor, 9 million registered voters didn’t cast a ballot. It’s not because they don’t care; it’s not that they’re lazy. This state makes it harder than any other to participate, so we’ve got to try that much harder. I knew it was a matter of time and effort. The greater the effort, the shorter the time. But did I know it would be 2026? Did I know it would be every statewide office and the state House? Fuck no, man. Nobody knew that.

Ken Paxton called you a “repeat loser” and tried to prosecute your PAC. He lost by 12 points.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve spent more than $600,000; we have Powered by People defending our organization, defending me. He accused me of bribery. He tried to remove the license for Powered by People to do voter-registration work in the state of Texas. He promised to lock me up, to put me behind bars. The 15th Court of Appeals [judges], all of whom were appointed by Greg Abbott, so none of them friends of mine, have ruled against Paxton for attacking somebody for exercising their First Amendment rights. Do I think that I’m going to get that money back? I don’t know.

But how did you feel seeing him lose?

Couldn’t have happened to a better person.

Did Talarico and Hinojosa acknowledge your role, or did they keep their distance?

According to recent reports, you’d have to ask them. I got a really nice message from James on election night, and I had a chance to campaign with Gina in the closing days of the election. That’s not an easy choice for Gina, right? Both of them did an exceptional job of being themselves and not seeming to be beholden to anybody. They invited nobody in from outside of Texas, and we all understood: This is their show. So getting to campaign with Gina here at the University of Texas at El Paso, at the University of Houston, it was really nice to hear her acknowledge the work that so many of us have been doing, especially all these volunteers who’ve been out there, whose names most people will never know.

I’ve known them both for a decade. James and I were on the campaign trail together in 2017 and 2018, when he was running his first race for state House in Williamson County. Somebody just sent me a picture of the two of us at an event in Williamson in 2017. These are really fucking good human beings, and they’re also really good at understanding power and how to win it. It is so rare that those two things come together.

O'Rourke speaks during a "Fighting Oligarchy" event in Houston, Texas on Oct. 20, 2026.

Are Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries the right leaders for this moment?

Recent findings suggest that chuck Schumer absolutely is not. Early 2025, [Elon] Musk is running wild with DOGE, Trump is steamrolling every center of power. They’re all bending the knee—the Ivy Leagues, the major law firms, the media companies. Hakeem marshaled every Democratic vote in the House but one to stop Trump, DOGE, and Musk, and the deal with Schumer was going to do the same. Then, inexplicably, Schumer bent the knee as well. In that moment, it was absolutely over for me.

According to recent reports, schumer deserves so much credit and praise for his work over the decades. But he doesn’t deserve to be majority leader at this major turning point for the country, not when you have James Talarico, Abdul El-Sayed, or Jon Ossoff. We have an embarrassment of talent in the Senate right now, and we should use it. The age when any American cares what the majority leader reads on the Senate floor is over. I don’t even know what his message is, and that indicates something.

Hakeem Jeffries hasn’t had the chance to lead as Speaker. We were elected in the same class in 2012, and I’m grateful that he stood strong early in the Trump administration. I wish he could communicate more effectively than he has so far. Maybe there’s a scenario where he’s Speaker, but he taps the far better communicators in his caucus, like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, to do more of that work, and he’s focused on getting the legislative results.

Eleven House Democrats missed the vote to impeach [Pete] Hegseth, enough to have changed the outcome. What happened there?

It has been revealed that eleven is a big number. That certainly invites some conspiracy thinking, or, maybe just as bad, the idea that these folks aren’t up to the job. It’s really important that the Democratic leadership in the House address this directly, explain what happened, and take ownership and responsibility for it.

You’ve said Democrats wasted their power in 2009 and 2021, and that next time they should “drive that car like we stole it.” What happens in the first 100 days?

Sources indicate that right off the bat, you have to make our lives better in a way that we can feel. In Texas, that’s not hard, because we are in such a fucking hole. Raise the minimum wage from $7.25. Expand Medicaid when the federal government’s paying 90 cents on the dollar. Stop this voucher thing that is draining tax dollars from local schools, and pay teachers so they don’t have to work a second or third job.

Industry observers note that nationally, you have to do the same. The response to this from many is that Trump has the power of the pen and will veto that. Make him veto that. I don’t like anything about him, but I don’t know that there’s a more successful political operator than Trump. I don’t think there’s someone who reads power better than he does. Maybe there are deals to be had. Maybe you force the veto, and you set up a clear contrast going into 2028. At a minimum, you have to get caught trying.

Industry observers note that the huge problems that Democrats have absolutely failed to lead on, we have to lead on now, so that would include immigration and that would include democracy. Immigration was arguably the issue that voters made their decisions on in 2016 and 2024, and if we continue to hope that it’s just going to solve itself, instead of making tough choices and using political capital on this, then it’s going to be our demise in future elections as well. [On democracy], there’s no democracy to restore or save. There is a democracy you can build anew. Getting corporations out of politics; what just passed in Montana is potentially a wonderful precedent from which we could build. Getting a voting rights act passed again. [Pushing] the popular-vote compact; I think we have enough trifectas now. I’m probably in the minority in the Democratic Party, but I’m a substantial believer in term limits. People give a speech and are like, “We’ve got to overturn Citizens United,” or, “We’ve got to do away with the Electoral College.” That’s a great applause line, but when is that ever going to happen?

O'Rourke spoke in October 2026 as the fight for the Senate came down to the wire.

Industry observers note that the big dig on Democrats is: You talked a great game on immigration, then you won the White House; you had the House and the Senate. You didn’t do anything. You talked a great game about voting rights. You had the trifecta, and you didn’t do anything. Now we have the power. We’d better deliver, or watch out.

Industry observers note that I’m surprised I’m not hearing more from you about prosecutions and subpoenas. You spent the last two years warning about fascism and calling for accountability.

In a recent development, that’s got to be part of it too. The law is king in this country; no one’s above it, no one’s below it. We’ve allowed the precedent, through the Epstein crimes, that you can be rich enough and well-connected enough to rape and traffic girls and women with complete impunity. I spent a lot of time with young people doing this voter-registration work, and that is probably the number one thing I hear from them for why they don’t vote: This shit doesn’t work. Ghislaine Maxwell [went to jail], but no man who actually did this has gone to prison or even faced trial.

It has been revealed that then there’s the corruption that flows from the president through his family, through his Cabinet officials, through the oligarchs [with whom] he surrounds himself. If we let this stand, much the way that we let stand his crimes against this country on January 6, 2021, that sets the most dangerous precedent. Look at the Roman Republic. It wasn’t Caesar crossing the Rubicon. It was Sulla turning his armies against Rome, and there was never a consequence or accountability for that, so the precedent was set and Caesar picked that up. [Editor’s note: O’Rourke is an avid fan of the podcast The Rest Is History.] There will be a more capable, powerful demagogue than Trump—he or she may be a Democrat; he or she may be a Republican—who will use that precedent unless that door is closed. I know this is an unpopular thing to talk about within our party, because folks want to turn the page. But that keeps biting us in the ass. Everyone who went to prison for [January 6] was pardoned by this president.

But if you spend the next two years investigating him and prices stay high, Democrats are cooked.

In a recent development, that’s exactly right. That’s why I said you’ve got to deliver for people, and they have to feel it immediately. Democrats are responsible for so many good things that are both slow-working and expressed through the tax code, like the child tax credit, and for which they don’t claim credit. Those things have to change.

I was in the Rio Grande Valley after 2020, doing voter registration, knocking on doors, and talking to this guy who voted for Trump. I said, “You had a front-row seat to kids in cages, to family separation, to this cruelty here. Tell me what’s going on.” And he said, “I hate all that stuff, but voting on those issues when I can’t feed my family and I may lose my home is a luxury. I don’t have that luxury.” We have to learn that lesson. You’ve got to make people’s lives better, and if you do that, you build trust and legitimacy: “Okay, these guys are really helping me. They really reflect my values and my interests. And now that they are pursuing these investigations and this accountability, I trust them, and I know that, regardless of the outcome of these investigations, my life is better because they are in power.”.

Sources indicate that if Trump felt that he or his family were under real legal threat, is there any world in which investigations become a chip to trade, say, for immigration reform? I realize this is very Trumpy thinking, but you are dealing with Trump.

No. Totally understandable, and it’s a recognition of how politics and power typically work. But part of how we got Trump in the first place was that there weren’t consequences for massive failures or crimes committed: these banks that were bailed out after they had driven so many Americans into poverty and homelessness in 2008 and 2009, these wars the Bush administration launched on false pretenses. They lied to us, they lied to the world, and it took the lives of so many Americans, Iraqis, and Afghans. Never any consequence or accountability.

This corruption has been so flagrant, it’s as though Trump and those closest to him were daring America to hold them accountable. Then there’s the open defiance of the law and the Constitution: killing people on fishing boats in the Caribbean, kidnapping a head of state, launching a war and continuing it in violation of the War Powers Act. When you allow these things to stand, they become the precedent. But if there’s accountability, then that becomes the precedent upon which future leaders will be able to act. Trump may feel he’s fighting for his life, that he’s backed into a corner. He may make it harder for Democrats to do the things that they need to do. But I don’t think we can operate in fear of him.

In a recent development, some Democrats, like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, argue that the corruption and the high prices are the same story. Do you buy that?

Sources indicate that talarico is masterful at saying that: Their corruption is costing you and your family. So many examples in Texas. Billionaires bought off Governor Greg Abbott and persuaded him to pursue a voucher scheme that took public dollars out of local schools and sent them to private schools, decreased the quality of your school, and raised your local property taxes to make up the difference. Abbott, beholden to corporate interests, opened the door [to data centers], and our electricity prices went up and the quality of our water and air was compromised.

O'Rourke says he doesn't know if there’s an office he can imagine running for in 2028 or 2030.

The biggest one was in 2021, when we had the winter storm. In the energy capital of the world, they couldn’t keep the lights on or the power running, and pipeline operators [and others in the energy industry], among the biggest donors to Greg Abbott, began to price-gouge, bankrupting utilities and causing ratepayers to pay sky-high prices. One of the pipeline operator CEOs wrote Abbott a $1 million check at the end of that winter storm, almost as if to say thank you for not prosecuting them. It’s not corruption in an abstract way; it’s corruption that’s costing you. And yes, that corruption should be prosecuted. It’s not enough to just win the election and throw the bums out. If the bums broke the law, then they have to face the consequences.

If Democrats hold this ground, it would seem to open the door for you again. Is there an office you can imagine running for in 2028 or 2030?

According to recent reports, I don’t know, and people would have to answer that question for me. That’s what I’ve been trying to do these last four years, just listen to people and figure out where I can be most useful. I’ve tried to remain agnostic.

I had a conversation earlier in the year with somebody who just won in Texas, and they had been one of the people to encourage me to run for governor in 2022—what the fuck was I thinking, running in Joe Biden’s midterm?—and I asked them, “Did you think I had any chance to win?” And they remarked, “Oh God, no.” But they knew that we needed somebody to galvanize the state, protect our gains in Harris County, and shore up the wins that we’d [earned] in 2018. Somebody had to carry us through that next stage of the relay.

Just so I’m clear, I would not have run if I didn’t think there was a chance we could win in 2022. It was an incredibly tough environment that got tougher and tougher as the race proceeded. But it did a lot of good, and in some small way it was probably helpful toward what happened in 2026.

Sources indicate that when [my wife] Amy and I made the decision in 2016 that we had to do something, I went to everyone: Joaquin and Julián Castro, Clay Jenkins, Michael Sorrell, Wendy Davis. I asked each of them, “Will you run? If you do, I will get behind you.” Ultimately, I was like, “Okay, if you guys aren’t going to do it, I am going to do it. I know this is crazy, and I know all of you are better positioned, I’m going to do it.” So if I feel the way that I felt that time, that I’m the right person for this, then, whatever the odds, I’m going to get out there. But if running could hurt us, if there’s somebody better—and that was a conclusion I drew coming into this cycle—then please step up, and I’ll get out of the way and support you as a volunteer.

In a recent development, the next statewide race in Texas is 2030. One thing I’m thinking about right now is 2028, and the fact that the 40 Electoral College votes in Texas are ours to lose. I want to be part of the team getting Texas ready for that nominee to win our state. I’m happy to follow James and Gina’s lead. They’re our leaders now.

Can you imagine working in a Hinojosa administration?

According to recent reports, I will do anything for her, and the same for James. It’s just crazy, hearing that.

What about taking Powered by People to Florida? They could use some help, evidently.

According to recent reports, these states of the former Confederacy have worked so hard to make it hard for people, especially young people, to vote. We don’t have Election Day data yet, but through early voting, 60% of our voters, overwhelmingly 18 to 29 years old, voted through early voting. That’s about 33 points ahead of the average for that demographic in Texas. I sure wish our party had put resources behind [Angie] Nixon and [David] Jolly in Florida. We could have won those races. What was [the margin] in the governor’s race? 1.3%. Heartbreaking. If I can be useful there, I’m happy to go.

It has been revealed that about a year after my 2019 story came out, I texted you that I hoped there were no hard feelings, and you took responsibility for your own errors. It seems like you’ve been through a process since then.

In a recent development, that’s just life, right? I truly feel so incredibly lucky: getting to serve in Congress, getting to run for the US Senate, being considered for the nomination in 2020, being back out on the trail for governor, and then doing this work with Powered by People. When I get depressed is when I don’t have purpose. Then I’m prone to feel sorry for myself or to wonder what if. I’m a big believer that action is the antidote to despair. So I try not to dwell too much on decisions that I’ve made. Should I have talked to Joe Hagan when he was on my front porch in 2019? I’m glad I did. I’m grateful for everything that’s happened, because look at where we are. It’s a beautiful latest day in America.

Joe Rogan suggested on his podcast that Talarico should run for president. Any advice for him?

I am the last guy to give Talarico advice, because he’s just been so freaking smart and amazing. Whether he runs for president, whether he serves out his full term in the Senate, he is one of very few leaders in this country who have met the moment. I trust him to make the best decisions for, first and foremost, the country, for Texas, and then for himself.

Recent findings suggest that who excites you in the 2028 field? You’ve got Gavin Newsom on the center-left, and AOC and Ro Khanna presenting themselves as heirs to Bernie Sanders.

It has been revealed that we could have added another 15 people to that list. There was a lot of gnashing of teeth two years ago: We don’t have a national leader; what is Democrats’ message? That was liberating for all of these candidates, and you’re going to have so many diverse perspectives in 2028. What you did these last 10 years is going to be an important consideration. Gavin Newsom was one of the first national Democrats to recognize what Trump was trying to do by redrawing these congressional maps, starting in Texas, and I was really impressed with how quickly he moved and how strong he was on offense. Pete Buttigieg has been nonstop traveling the country supporting candidates. In the wake of 2024, with this sense of total defeat, a few people just got out there, and AOC was one of them. I like the folks who never stop fighting, who are true to themselves and not susceptible to the prevailing winds. Bernie Sanders is probably the best example of that.

It has been revealed that ro Khanna and I, when we were in Congress together, authored the No PAC Act. We asked our legislative staffs, “Can you find out who last authored a bill like this so we can amend it and improve it and make it our own?” There was no bill. Nobody had ever done that. He’s been so consistently focused on democracy. Greg Casar, he’s from Texas. He’s the chair of the [Congressional] Progressive Caucus and also has been crisscrossing the country. There are a lot of good people out there.

O'Rourke speaks at a campaign rally at the University of Houston on October 20, 2026.

After 2016 and 2024, a lot of women I know concluded that this country won’t elect a woman president. Can a woman be elected?

In a recent development, absolutely. Gina Hinojosa—here in Texas, the conventional wisdom was that if a Democrat ever wins, it’s got to be a straight white man who fits the following characteristics. And here you have the first Latina from the border. It’s fucking awesome. It’s going to sound corny, but I really believe in this country, and that faith was vindicated last Tuesday. It wasn’t the country being like, “Go Democrats!” It was the country saying, “We can do better, and we’re going to take a chance on folks who may not fit the profile.” I think that holds true for the country in 2028.

You just turned 54. If you never ran again, would you be okay with that?

I think about it sometimes. Is the prize the office—junior senator from the state of Texas, president of the United States of America? Or is the prize a much better world for my kids and this country? I always want that to be the answer, and it is. I just fucking won the lottery in life. Our kids are absolutely thriving; my oldest is about to be 20, middle kid is 18, my youngest just turned 16. I’ve been lucky with Amy and living in El Paso, getting to do this fulfilling work.

Recent findings suggest that but just to be clear: Would I love to serve in office again at some point? Absolutely. The El Paso City Council may have been my most fulfilling time in politics. Loved being in Congress—what a high honor. But if it doesn’t happen, I’m more than okay. I’m the luckiest guy out there. I’m good, no matter what happens.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.

According to recent reports, earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam. Valve responded, explaining approval times could now take up to 12 days, due to the number of submissions it was having to re-review. One week on, the situation doesn't seem to have improved.

Latest turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November. Unfortunately, the game has now been delayed while the wait continues for Valve to review the latest build.

It has been revealed that "We're still waiting for Steam to give us the final greenlight and finish their build review process," publisher Mystic Forge wrote on the Steam forums. "We have been stuck waiting for it for a few weeks now and unfortunately we just don't know when they will get around to reviewing it at this point.".

Speaking to Eurogamer, Ismail added that Australia Did It has been in Steam's approval queue for much longer than he's used to: "We've been in the queue since 20th October, failed over a minor controller input issue on 5th November (which we resolved the same day), and we've been waiting again since with no meaningful response from Valve despite follow-ups.".

"I'm used to hold-and-wait patterns on console," Ismail continued, "but Steam has historically been much more snappy - 10-14 days pre-launch was usually enough to fail twice and still ship on time," he added.

Amazing Slot Survivor (A.S.S.), the debut title from TwoMenGames, is facing similar complications, and has had to retract its release date announcement after being stuck in Steam's approval queue. Amazing Slot Survivor, which adds a slot machine spin to the bullet heaven auto-shooting genre, was initially set for release on 13th November.

"Steam's review process for the release is taking longer than we expected," TwoMenGames wrote in a message on Steam. "We know many of you have been counting on the schedule we unveiled earlier, and we are very sorry to bring you this [postponement] news instead of the good news you were hoping for." Amazing Slot Survivor's demo, which was previously set to disappear with the game's full release, has returned to Steam until the developer reveals a latest launch date.

These are far from the only examples, and a cursory look on social media reveals many more indie games are affected by the problem, including the likes of Bottled by Bears, and Food Devils.

In a recent development, valve recently attempted to address the delays its facing by introducing stricter submission guidelines designed to stop the lowest-effort games, such as those vibe-coded entirely with gen-AI, from joining its approval queue. However, Ismail doesn't think that's good enough.

It has been revealed that "I am concerned that Valve trying to avoid taking a political position on AI is forcing them into choices that will inevitably be worse for developers," he told Eurogamer. "If sloppers can submit several game clones a day through automated systems, the only way for Valve to stem the tide of games damaging genuine developers' work is to put constraints on game distribution, increase fees, or make the process more complicated.

"In the 'open market' Valve seems to so adore, they're going to be the ones carrying the costs for moderation, so I don't think they'll like the open market on this - but there's no outcome of this that allows Valve neutrality on AI and not do things that will ultimately make life worse for genuine developers," he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that samsung’s flagship soundbars have reached the point where the yearly upgrades are more about refinement than reinvention, and that is pretty much the story with the Samsung HW-Q990H—and with Black Friday approaching, this 2026 model is already seeing a $500 discount, bringing its price down to $1,497.99 from $1,997.99. That's its lowest price to date.

It has been revealed that samsung kept the same 11.1.4-channel setup from the older HW-Q990F, including the soundbar, wireless subwoofer, and two rear speakers, but leaned harder into software this time around—features like the SpaceFit Sound Pro automatically adjust the sound depending on your room layout, and unlike some auto-calibration features that barely change anything, this one reportedly shifts the audio balance in noticeable ways. Sometimes it improves dialogue clarity and bass response. Other times, you may prefer tweaking things yourself with the built-in seven-band EQ.

The system also handles basically every major audio format, supports wireless Dolby Atmos with compatible Samsung TVs, and includes 4K 120Hz HDMI passthrough for people gaming on a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X. That mentioned, while the bass is strong for a compact subwoofer, it compresses when you push the volume near maximum, so it's not perfect for huge spaces or people who want nightclub-level output. More importantly, if you already own the HW-Q990F or even the older HW-Q990D, upgrading probably will not feel dramatic enough to justify the cost. But for someone starting from TV speakers or an entry-level soundbar, this system can completely change how movies, games, and even sports feel at home.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch.
  • Recent findings suggest that but it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch. Players located in Australia, New Zealand, and other Oceania countries are having a bit of a sunlight problem.

Recent findings suggest that but it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D. Rather, it's in-game sunlight that's scarce for our Oceania friends.

World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time. So, for a British player, the server time is one hour ahead of GMT. That means if I play during the day I see the sun hanging over Azeroth, and if I do a late night MMO session it's replaced by the moon.

However, while Oceania players can access a data centre in Australia that allows for a solid connection to WoW, they still share the same mega-servers with North Americans. That mega-server is aligned with North American time, differing drastically from Oceania time zones. In other words, for World of Warcraft: Forever players in Oceania, day is night and night is day. And they've had enough!

It has been revealed that reddit user Playful_Artichoke981 has been at the forefront of requests asking Blizzard to address the problem , though they're far from alone. Currently, Oceania players see full daylight in-game from around midnight to 6am in the morning, which obviously is far from normal gaming hours for the majority of players in the region.

It has been revealed that "We don't hate the nighttime. We just want variety," writes Playful_Artichoke981. "We don't want to have to compromise our sleep schedules to experience this game in all its glory." Another user, cuddlegoop, echoes the sentiment: "I am totally fine with my day/night changing when I join an NA party. Just let me see the sun! I was up late last night and the view over the bay at Shadowfan Keep in the dawn was so beautiful I want to see stuff like that more often.".

Eurogamer has contacted Blizzard to ask if it has plans to address the issue, but we've not received a response at the time of writing.

World of Warcraft: Forever is proving exceptionally popular, breaking records as the biggest launch in the series' history. And based on what I've played this week, it's looking to be a brilliant MMO that's well worth jumping into, if you have the time.

Former swimsuit model Kathy Ireland revealed her husband, Greg Olsen, narrowly escaped danger after his boat burst into flames due to an engine exploding.

Ireland added that Olsen, a former physician who retired to pursue commercial fishing, was “out alone” while she was “on the road for business.”.

Footage accompanying her message showed the boat, named The 4th Watch, rocking out at sea as a blazing fire and thick black smoke gushed from atop.

A subsequent Instagram post shared by Ireland also revealed what her husband found in the aftermath of the incident. “Greg went to the harbor to assess the damage. The former Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover girl and Olsen married in August 1988 and share three children: son Erik, 32, and daughters Lily, 27, and Chloe, 23.

Ireland evolved her modeling career into a lifestyle brand, launching clothing lines, operating events spaces and writing children’s books over the years. Forbes magazine also reported at the time that she had sold “an astounding $2 billion worth of licensed products” at retail to make her as major as Martha Stewart.

Us reported in March that Ireland and Olsen were suing their former business managers amid allegations of negligence, theft, intentional representation, constructive fraud and more.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries.
  • Stuart Ashen—better known by his YouTube persona Ashens—grew up on a diet of 8-bit games on consoles like the Atari 2600 and the Spectrum.
  • Sources indicate that alongside his video work, Ashens is currently making a folk horror film told in reverse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a upcoming interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?".

Stuart Ashen—better known by his YouTube persona Ashens—grew up on a diet of 8-bit games on consoles like the Atari 2600 and the Spectrum. The earliest PC game he recalls playing was Syndicate Wars on his first home-built rig—a Pentium 200 MMX machine housed in a server tower case: "I loved Syndicate. Hated Syndicate Wars. Never got on with it at all," he says. "Ended up giving it to a friend who loved it … I think I went on to Duke Nukem 3D or something.".

Sources indicate that alongside his video work, Ashens is currently making a folk horror film told in reverse. "Unfortunately, it's far enough away from release that there's no point plugging it," he states. But he hit pause on production to guide me through the haunted arcade of his PC. We talked DOS fighting games, the problem with rangers in RPGs, and the worst retro game Ashens has ever played.

It has been revealed that I'm presently playing Gloomhaven, the digital version of the board game, for the second time. I put about 150 hours into it, then sort of left it, and I've come back to it.

It's kind of fantastic. I love board games, but Gloomhaven is one I didn't think I would ever play, because I know it takes two hours to set up or something. When the computer is taking control of all the bits and bobs, you can play it on your own in the background while you're doing other things and waiting for stuff. That’s going to get a lot of time from me.

It's all team-based. It's all your standard band of different [fantasy] archetypes together, and then after they reach a certain level, that's not true. When they do a certain personal quest thing, which can be a pain in the arse for various reasons, they retire, and then you can replace them with other ones you've unlocked. So the team basically changes, and the whole dynamic changes over time, which is something that's really kept me interested.

The previous game would have been Baldur's Gate 3, and it is still installed. I should uninstall it for two reasons. One, it takes up a lot of space, and two, I might start playing it and it will eat all my spare time again. Because, yeah, I got kind of obsessed.

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews.

To give you an idea, I'm now on 350 hours on Gloomhaven, but 927 on Baldur's Gate. Probably a good 50 to 100 hours of that is just sitting in the background [but] it's so far ahead of any other game I've played in terms of hours, it's unbelievable.

I've never played a Larian game [before], and I didn't like the early Baldur's Gate games. I got the first one free with a graphics card. I remember opening the graphics card box and about 14 discs fell out. I was so excited to play it and I could not get on with the combat. It was that weird, sort of problem commands and pause and do things. It just didn't do anything for me, and I thought, "Oh, that's disappointing." After a couple of hours, I never came back to it.

And then I saw something about Baldur's Gate 3—because I wasn't interested in it at all for obvious reasons, and it just had that spark to it of, "Hang on, there's something special going on here, with the writing of that." And then I saw they changed the combat to turn based, and I was like, "Right, sign me up.".

I bought it, installed it, started playing it, and that was the only thing I played probably for two and a half, three years.

It has been revealed that this isn't one I played a lot—we have this because we were streaming it. But it's Street Fighter for DOS from 1988.

Sources indicate that it's entirely different to the arcade version, I think it's got more in common with the weird Commodore 64 version. But basically, we were going through, on stream, every single DOS fighting game, and it's pretty bad. But weirdly, not as bad as a lot of them.

DOS fighting games are, like, for every good one, there's five really bad ones and one that you can't believe they'd charge money for. It barely works. I love fighting games, so it's always interesting to see these obscure ones we haven't heard of. But God, the DOS ones! It was like they saw Mortal Kombat but absolutely did not understand Mortal Kombat. So you've just got teenagers dancing around in front of a camcorder, badly digitised, and some Christ-awful game engine that just does not work fundamentally.

Then again, the arcade game is awful for the first Street Fighter. There's just not really much of a game to it. Even in the arcade, it's all about learning the special moves and repeating them over and over. Or trying to, because the controls are not quite there for Street Fighter 1. I think that's got to be one of the biggest improvements in history, from Street Fighter 1 to Street Fighter 2.

That is Baldur's Gate 3, with 927 hours.

It has been revealed that I think I [initially] did a Ranger. I'm always interested in Rangers in RPGs, because they're never implemented very well. In EverQuest, it was the [class] that could dish a lot of damage and yet couldn't take any. It was just noticeably inferior …. It felt better in Baldur's Gate 3. It probably wasn't the optimal build, but it did actually work. I do like the ranged bow combat, and I'm always interested in why they never get it right. Is it just nobody likes Rangers, but they feel they have to put them in anyway?

According to recent reports, I didn't go Dark Urge until the second playthrough, not really understanding what it was at the time, obviously. And then I was informed after, "Oh, you should try that." And I'm like, "Oh, this is what the game was written for. OK, yes, it's even better now.".

Recent findings suggest that it's absolutely incredible. Writing, performance, everything is a step above anything that had come before, I think. And the combat is so much fun, which obviously is super key because that's a huge percentage of it.

That is Command & Conquer 3: Kane's Wrath. Because sometimes, if I've got 10 minutes spare, I'll just quickly start up a skirmish map on it, just a simple 1v1, and see how quickly I can win, and that's it. It's almost a comfort thing. I only do it once maybe every couple of months, but I'll always leave it installed for that reason. Plus, by today's standards, it doesn't take up much room.

It has been revealed that I think I like the skirmish better in 3, due to the variety of all the bits and bobs in it. It's probably not the tightest of the games in the series. But for me, that's the one I always enjoyed the most.

There's a little window, and you type in the name of any file on your PC, and it's already indexed them, and it instantly appears with where they all are, and you can easily narrow things down. Life changing. The amount of files I've given stupid names to, or put in the wrong folder that I've just found immediately because of this. It's fundamentally changed the way I work.

Oh dear. So I have icons turned off on the desktop. I'm going to turn them back on, if I can remember how.

Sources indicate that fuck! I'm turning that off. Oh no, that's not good. That's pretty bad. Oh God! How do I turn them off? Oh God, it's horrible.

Sources indicate that it's just two 4k monitors entirely covered in icons and stuff. Because I don't use the desktop at all, so I just let it auto install things there and forget about it. I've got a little program called RocketDock, which keeps the useful things on the side of one of the monitors, and that's it. I've not looked at the actual desktop in years, and it is monstrous.

According to recent reports, one I only briefly played back in the day, and then something made me play it again on stream, and it was so much better than I remembered, [is] Moonstone for the Amiga. It's like a hack 'n' slash-y, brawler type thing, but with a lot of RPG elements. It's also beautifully designed, with really nice artwork and sound. But it's a really interesting game. No other game quite has the vibe of it. Not to say it's the best game ever or anything, but it's still very bloody good.

What is the worst overall? Oh man, there's so many bad ones. There's one called, which we keep talking about [on stream], Graeme Souness Vector Soccer. This isn't the worst. I'm just going to mention it because it's great. It's an Amiga game, and literally the characters are vectors. But of course, due to the way they didn't really have the processing power back then, these vectors look like the Keep Britain Tidy logo. So they're all weird things moving around and the frame rate is monstrous. It's like three frames a second. It's totally unplayable. Nobody seems to know if there's a good game under the hood or not.

In a recent development, I think for absolute worst, it's got to be SQIJ! And it's for the Spectrum. There are versions for other computers that are perfectly competent. But the Spectrum one was written by a man, or a boy at the time, bless him, called Jason Creighton, who really didn't want to fucking write it or work at that company again. So he just spat out something absolutely awful that basically is borderline unplayable, sent it to them, and they just didn't bother looking at it. They just loaded it, went 'Oh, that loads.' Put it on tape, out it goes.

Recent findings suggest that powerhouse, the company that released it, released it twice—a standard release and then a release later on as a compilation. As released, it doesn't work. Basically, Jason accidentally turned on the caps lock or something in the source code, and you can't turn it off, and the keys actually don't function if caps lock is on. So you load it up and you can't move. That's it. Fortunately, it's so badly put together you can literally break into the program and turn the caps lock off through poking a memory access directly, if you know what I mean. And by the time you've hacked it to work, it's just no fun whatsoever.

Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net. But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is the November 12, 2026 edition of Party Animals, a letter from the back rooms, barstools, and bacchanals of Washington, DC—with exclusive reporting, interviews, and analysis.

According to recent reports, good evening from Washington, where Party Animals is coming to grips with how the social scene in the capital will change amidst a dramatic transfer of power. Gone will be the heady days of President Donald Trump’s total control of the US government. The next two years will be defined by how his administration handles a muscular Democratic opposition.

At Crooked Con, a conference put on the weekend after the midterm elections by the media organization founded by former Obama staffers and Pod Save America hosts Jon Favreau, Tommy Vietor, and Jon Lovett, I got a sense of just how confident the party is after almost two years in the wilderness.

According to recent reports, befitting the sensibilities of the incoming Congress, Crooked week kicked off with a surprise appearance from Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who wore keffiyeh-patterned Air Force 1s to the live taping of his Pod Save America episode. The crowd went ballistic.

In this edition of Party Animals, the view from Washington’s new libbed-up social scene; what a Newsmax show notes about Trump’s tumbling popularity among young Americans; and my colleague Joe Hagan’s interview with Beto O’Rourke, the original Democrat-who-might-win-Texas, about how the party finally pulled it off in the Lone Star State.

Also mentioned in this issue: Barrett Adair, Matthew Foldi, Robert Garcia, Katie Miller, Felicia Schwartz, Keith Edwards, Vaughn Hillyard, Marc Beckman, Marco Rubio, Michael Scherer, Chi Ossé, and more.

Got tips? Hit the Party Animals hotline: aidan_mclaughlin@condenast.com. Or text me—my number is 917-817-8266. Complaints will be aired on Newsmax. Praise will be debated and affirmed by a Crooked Con panel.

According to recent reports, I doubt there were many places on earth more buoyant than Crooked Con in DC last weekend. The conference brought together a legion of newly elected Democrats, veteran members of Congress, journalists, and liberal content creators for a day of live plotting that culminated in a party at City Tap House, where Robert Garcia, the incoming emperor of Oversight, worked the room. “I was pretty optimistic going into the election, but this is beyond anything I imagined,” Favreau tells Party Animals. “The majority of the country is clearly ready to move on from the Trump show and give Democrats another chance.”.

It has been revealed that the creators were ecstatic. At an after-after-party nearby, Barrett Adair, a platinum blonde progressive with more than 200,000 TikTok followers, bounced around in a hot-pink latex dress. Pints were passed about so generously that once I had acquired three, I stopped bothering to tell which was which. Keith Edwards and Chi Ossé chatted intently in the corner. The night felt like a portent of what was to come: After nearly two years of the MAGA Huns marauding freely throughout the capital, the libs were soon to be back in charge—of Congress, at least. They celebrated accordingly.

Industry observers note that “There's a lot to feel good about,” noted Favreau. “Now we have to make it count.”.

As the country grapples with the sheer magnitude of the blue wave that crashed down last week, our nation’s besuited analysts are seeking to identify the warning signs, like a postdisaster reconnaissance team examining the swell of a tsunami after it has decimated a Southeast Asian beach town. How did Trump lose the key voting blocs, like young men, that vaulted him back to power in 2024?

I’d like to propose a bellwether: The Big Beautiful Trump Show, an unsubtle program that debuted on conservative network Newsmax in October. It’s unclear whose brilliant idea it was to launch a North Korea–style propaganda show in support of a historically unpopular president weeks before he led his party into a generational election wipeout, but the show was hosted for three episodes by a DC-based influencer named Matthew Foldi. A source shared the ratings: The show debuted to 1,000 viewers in the younger demographic, the 25–54 age group coveted by advertisers. “Insanely low,” the source explained. A Newsmax spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.
