📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem are very selective about when they work on a project together, but the opportunity to costar in director Florian Zeller's timely psychological thriller Bunker was too enticing to pass up.

In a recent development, "When [Zeller] came to us with this powerful, very necessary story to tell, we looked at each other and there was no way to say no to this," Cruz mentioned during a post-screening discussion at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room on Sunday. "I'm very, very happy that we did it.".

Bunker revolves around a married couple, Miguel (Bardem) and Sofia (Cruz), whose 17-year marriage is tested when Miguel, a famous architect, is presented with a life changing work opportunity.

Industry observers note that “I really wanted to work with them because I truly believe they are [two] of the greatest actors working today,” Zeller said during the panel discussion moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross. “I was also very excited and interested to have them together onscreen because they are also a real couple. I thought it would be an interesting and unique opportunity to approach something that has to do with authenticity, with the truth. Not to say that this is their story, because of course this is not their story.”.

Florian Zeller at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

In a recent development, cruz said she felt a kinship with her character's concerns. “We have so many things in common in terms of this sadness and frustration and anger that you feel in terms of where is the world going if we don't wake up soon,” she said. “I hope it's not too late, but especially the experiment that is being done on younger people, children, teenagers, it just makes me very furious.

“It's something that affects me so much as an actress, as a mother, as a citizen of the world, that I felt completely a need to play Sophia,” she continued. “And of course it was not the only reason, but it was a significant privilege to be able to say those lines. And [Zeller] is such a master of writing and I am a fan of all his work. And same for Javier, who is not here with us today, he's doing theater, but we are very careful in terms of choosing when to work together.”.

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

Industry observers note that cruz praised Zeller’s ability to provide a supportive, safe working environment and his strong point of view. “We felt really, really safe with him, he's so talented. He doesn't need any kind of manipulation and he never treats the audience as not intelligent because the audience can feel everything,” she explained. “And that has become really the most important thing for me. Don't over-explain, don't underestimate the audience ever because the thermometer is really working. And also with young people more and more and more. That is my hope to continue to go to see films on a substantial screen. They're coming back thank God. So let's create more possibilities so they can keep doing that.”.

Recent findings suggest that cruz also said that she and Bardem have similar approaches to their work and the preparation it requires. “It's true that we share the same passion and we have done this since we were teenagers,” she said. “We love exploring and studying and feeling that healthy fear of the unknown because every time you begin a project, in a way, it's really starting from zero. So it's a really good thing to share.”.

Zeller called his collaboration with the couple “a fascinating journey. It takes a lot of courage or fearlessness to do that, I think, for actors.” He also revealed that he initially referenced Stanley Kubrick's seminal thriller Eyes Wide Shut as a point of reference for Bunker, but realized it might not be setting the proper tone, given the circumstances.

According to recent reports, “I remember that the first time I spoke with [Cruz] and Javier about this project, I mentioned a film that was somewhere in my mind, Eyes Wide Shut. Not to say that there is any kind of connection between the two films, but as you remember, Eyes Wide Shut at the time, Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman, they were together," he noted. "And I remember as a viewer that it was so interesting to be in a position where you do not know exactly what you're invited to watch… but Javier [later] told me, ‘You should not mention this film too often because remember at the end of the shooting they broke up.’ And then I realized that the director, Kubrick, died soon after. So I was like, ‘Okay, I'm going to stop mentioning this film.’ But the real difference I would say is that we knew that the destination of that film was the last image of the painting that you saw, which means that it was about how to reconnect with the other.”.

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026.

Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. As shared on the forum ResetEra, users who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F7LIovDySBg&t=33s In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6. At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will update this post if and when we receive a response. If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80, you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group.

Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick, a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin.

According to recent reports, A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital, where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger.

It has been revealed that as we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft, Samsung, Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Kurtaj was also reportedly violent while in hospital custody, causing "dozens" of reports of injuries or property damage. In July 2026, that 'no longer a danger' determination was presumably made, as Kurtaj was released from hospital and moved to prison to await retrial.

Industry observers note that he has now pleaded guilty to multiple hacks carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, including the Rockstar hack that led to the GTA 6 leak. He also pleaded guilty to assaults on workers while in custody, which the BBC report says included "multiple biting incidents.".

As I mentioned when Kurtaj was moved from hospital to prison, the whole thing strikes me as odd. The major question is how Kurtaj's state of mind at the time of the crimes will influence the outcome of his guilty plea, given that a previous court determined that he needed multiple years of institutionalization. BBC tech reporter Joe Tidy, who's been following the case since Kurtaj's transfer, also described it as "an unusual move" in his report.

According to recent reports, coincidentially, one must assume, Grand Theft Auto 6 debuts for consoles on November 19. Kurtaj will be sentenced at a future date. The leaker who goes by Cyberleek, who recently distributed several GTA 6 gameplay videos apparently taken with a development build of the game, remains at large.

From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from latest game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 rolls out on November 19. The game is poised to "blot out the sun," some experts believe, and its release looms so large that other gaming companies are shifting dates for their own games to stay out of the blast radius. Francis Lawrence, the director of the fresh Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has remarked he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play. To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research company PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics. He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself." Jason pumping some iron in GTA 6. Spiegel said he foresees potential shifts beyond gaming, in places like TV viewership, music consumption, social media engagement, and even travel. "In an increasingly fragmented entertainment landscape, it's rare for a single release to command this much attention across so many industries simultaneously. That's what makes this moment so significant," he said. An economics professor recently claimed that about 1.5 million people plan to "call out sick" to play GTA 6, and this could come at a "cost" of $1 billion to the US economy. Spiegel said people should remember that GTA 6 isn't anything new or special as it relates to taking time off work. "People regularly plan time off around major cultural and entertainment events, and this is another example of consumers prioritizing an experience they're excited about," he said. That being said, Spiegel remarked that PwC has observed estimates suggesting time-off requests near GTA 6's release could be 9% to 17% higher than normal. "But what's more interesting to me is what happens outside the workplace. If millions of people are spending additional hours gaming, they're potentially spending less time watching television, going out to restaurants, or engaging in other activities," he said. "And unlike a sporting event that lasts a few hours or a few weeks, this experience could keep people engaged for months. So the broader economic implications may extend well beyond a single day of missed work," he added. "Huge net positive" GTA 6 is expected to be an enormous success commercially--it's reportedly already sold 11 million units through pre-purchases, and that could rise to 25 million at launch. That would work out to $2 billion in revenue, which would cover the game's entire development budget and most of its marketing spend, Sensor Tower said. But many are also saying that GTA 6 represents the last of a dying breed, and that other publishers might learn all the wrong lessons from its success. Spiegel said GTA 6 is going to be a "huge net positive for the gaming industry as a whole," in part because its success will reiterate to the broader entertainment and media landscape that games are culturally significant. At the same time, Spiegel said he doesn't foresee a world in which other publishers try to replicate a blockbuster of this magnitude. "Very few organizations have the capital, expertise, and intellectual property required to support investments on this scale. These are extraordinary events, not necessarily repeatable business models," Spiegel said. If GTA 6 is the huge success it's projected to be, it could positively uplift the broader gaming ecosystem in a lot of ways, Spiegel continued. "It could attract new audiences, renew investor interest, and create opportunities across advertising, payments, technology, and content creation. The real lesson isn't that everyone needs to build the next billion-dollar game. It's that gaming is an increasingly powerful part of the entertainment economy, with opportunities that extend well beyond the games themselves," he said. Jason escaping the law in GTA 6. Some companies, like Ubisoft, see GTA 6 not as something to be strictly afraid of. CEO Yves Guillemot states, that's because the rising tide that is GTA 6 could help drive more people to gaming overall. In fact, Ubisoft is putting out a significant new revision for one of its biggest games, Rainbow Six Siege, right around GTA 6's launch. Mat Piscatella of Circana reminded people that not everyone wants to play GTA 6, and he pushed back against the theory that it's a bad business idea to launch a game near GTA 6. "The fear of many teams to put their game in the same window as GTA is completely overblown. GTA is going to be a massive game. Of course it is. It’s going to be a huge cultural event, but not every one of the 49 million people who own a PS5 or an Xbox Series in the US is going to be interested in that," he told GamesBeat. Could GTA 6 lead the push to more in-game ads? Spiegel went on to say that one additional follow-on effect from GTA 6 could be something that gamers might balk at but publishers and investors might salivate over. He said that if GTA 6 succeeds in the way people expect it to, and draw people into its world for tens--or even hundreds--of hours, that could demonstrate to the wider market that it's time for gaming, as an industry, to do more with advertising. "When millions of people are spending substantial amounts of time in interactive entertainment environments, it's natural for advertisers and investors to consider how they might participate," he said. Advertising for mobile and social games is already commonplace, but it's less present in the PC and console gaming market. There are examples, of course, as companies have already undertaken efforts to put ads into gaming with mixed results. Gamers rapidly revolted when EA put ads in a UFC game, prompting EA to pull them quickly to help quell the backlash. Despite that, EA recently announced the formation of a new EA Advertising division that will seek to put ads "directly into gameplay." That announcement didn't go over well, either, as fans pushed back against the idea of having to see ads in yet another place in their life. Other examples have been received more positively, or at least ambivalently, with a trucking company buying ad space in the American Truck Simulator series to help recruit staff. Lucia and Jason in GTA 6. Xbox, for its part, has big plans to put more ads in gaming. Xbox CSO Matthew Ball said advertising in console games could help with the "two-sided problem" that AAA gaming faces today. Development costs keep going up and up, and Ball said ads--as long as they're not overly in-your-face--could be a way to help developers make more money and solidify their business fundamentals. Of course, if these companies insert more ads into gaming, that doesn't mean they'll stop hawking things like DLC, microtransactions, and battle passes; they'll likely both happen in concert. As Spiegel sees it, though, if executed correctly, advertising could be a big boon for gaming. "What's particularly interesting is that the opportunity extends beyond placing advertisements inside games. There's an entire ecosystem of digital advertising infrastructure, technology, and services that could benefit as gaming continues to grow. I expect we'll see increasing interest in those opportunities, particularly from investors looking for exposure to gaming without taking on the considerable financial risks associated with developing blockbuster titles," he said. More investment During the COVID years, the gaming industry saw massive revenue and player growth as people, forced to stay inside due to stay-at-home orders, turned to games to pass the time, have fun, and connect with friends. At the same time, interest rates were historically low. The cost to borrow money was so attractive that publishers ramped up significantly. The COVID-era boost to gaming did not last, though, and the industry is now challenged, to say the least, with numerous developers cutting staff, cancelling projects, and scaling back in other ways. If GTA 6 is indeed a massive success, it could trigger renewed interest in gaming as an investment vehicle, Spiegel believes, but not necessarily exclusively for funding new games and studios. Instead, Spiegel said he foresees big investment growth for discrete elements of gaming, including advertising, payment services, and AI buildouts. "I absolutely think a release of this magnitude will get the attention of investors, corporate executives, and private equity firms. But I don't necessarily think that translates into another wave of billion-dollar game development," he said. "The economics of producing games at this scale are incredibly challenging, and very few organizations have the resources, expertise, and intellectual property necessary to justify those investments." "Instead, I think investors will increasingly ask how they can participate in the broader gaming ecosystem," Spiegel added. "That could mean opportunities in advertising, payment infrastructure, technology services, mobile gaming, or artificial intelligence applications that support game development." On the subject of AI, Spiegel said he believes it's a "particularly interesting variable" because it could, at least in theory, allow developers to work more efficiently and bring down costs. There is debate about whether or not this is a genuine reality or wishful thinking on the part of AI companies trying to sell their products and services. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, for example, recently told Business Insider that, despite Take-Two adopting AI products for some of its workflows, the company has not seen a material decrease in its cost structure. In fact, many theorize that AI-supported workflows will only make work more intense. For his part, Spiegel said AI in game development remains only an "emerging opportunity rather than a guaranteed outcome." "The longer-term impact may be less about creating another generation of massive blockbusters and more about directing investment toward the businesses and technologies that support the gaming economy," he said. Who should be afraid? A lot has already been said and written about publishers moving their release dates to avoid GTA 6, and Spiegel said he foresees dramatic possibilities for how GTA 6 could take the wind out of the sails of other entertainment near its launch. He said GTA 6 is not just a major gaming launch. Instead, he thinks it's an "event that could temporarily reshape how millions of consumers spend their time and money." "Streaming could be particularly vulnerable. Every hour someone spends gaming is potentially an hour they're not watching a television show or movie. And because this launch falls just before the holiday season, it could make it difficult for streaming services to match the exceptionally strong viewership numbers we saw last year," he said. The new Hunger Games movie, Sunrise on the Reaping, releases a day after GTA 6 comes out. Movie theaters could be tested, Spiegel said, and one highly anticipated film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, will be one to watch in particular. It comes to theaters on Friday, November 20, which is one day after GTA 6 releases. Director Francis Lawrence said he hopes fans find the time to play GTA 6 and go see his movie, but it remains to be seen what effect, if any, GTA 6's release will have on that film's performance at the box office. Spiegel said movie studios are banking on the belief that the theatrical experience "offers something consumers can't get from their living rooms."  There is a Thursday Night Football game happening on the same day that GTA 6 releases, with the Indianapolis Colts taking on the Houston Texans. Spiegel said the live-sports category overall could be "more resilient" because of its nature as an event happening live that fans of those teams, or fans of the NFL in general, feel compelled to watch live as it happens. A movie or TV show, meanwhile, is on-demand entertainment. GTA 6 is a hugely anticipated release, and it's poised to bring lapsed gamers back into the fold, but anyone who doesn't already have a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S should prepare themselves for sticker shock. That's because, for a variety of reasons, new consoles today are actually hundreds of dollars more expensive than they were when they introduced in 2020. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has frankly acknowledged, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't shaking in his boots about what this means for GTA 6. He thinks GTA 6 will be so good and so compelling that people will buy in no matter what. "I don’t think it will slow us down any because, you know, we’re delivering, we believe we’re delivering experiences that people want,” Zelnick said. “However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands." Who benefits? In terms of companies, products, people, and services that could benefit from the ripple effects of GTA 6's release, Spiegel said music associated with the game could surge in listening activity. This has already happened, as streams of Tom Petty's "Love Is A Long Road" surged after the first trailer for GTA 6 used the song back in 2023. More recently, Cliff Richard's 1976 hit "Devil Woman" indicated up in the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix, helping the song reach more people, including young people who maybe never even knew about the song. Spiegel said social media platforms could benefit from GTA 6's release as well, thanks to fans uploading gameplay clips, livestreams, and other forms of user-generated content inspired by GTA 6. Beyond this, the world of food delivery could see an uptick in activity as people opt to stay in to play GTA 6 (while in-person restaurants and other nightlife venues could take a hit). "The broader point is that the impact could extend into parts of the economy we don't traditionally associate with gaming," Spiegel said. "For business leaders, the question is whether they're competing with this cultural moment for consumer attention or finding ways to participate in it. He said GTA 6 is not just a major gaming launch. Instead, he thinks it's an "event that could temporarily reshape how millions of consumers spend their time and money.".

According to recent reports, "Streaming could be particularly vulnerable. Every hour someone spends gaming is potentially an hour they're not watching a television show or movie. And because this launch falls just before the holiday season, it could make it difficult for streaming services to match the exceptionally strong viewership numbers we saw last year," he said.

In a recent development, movie theaters could be tested, Spiegel said, and one highly anticipated film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, will be one to watch in particular. It comes to theaters on Friday, November 20, which is one day after GTA 6 releases. Director Francis Lawrence said he hopes fans find the time to play GTA 6 and go see his movie, but it remains to be seen what effect, if any, GTA 6's release will have on that film's performance at the box office. Spiegel said movie studios are banking on the belief that the theatrical experience "offers something consumers can't get from their living rooms.".

According to recent reports, there is a Thursday Night Football game happening on the same day that GTA 6 releases, with the Indianapolis Colts taking on the Houston Texans. Spiegel said the live-sports category overall could be "more resilient" because of its nature as an event happening live that fans of those teams, or fans of the NFL in general, feel compelled to watch live as it happens. A movie or TV show, meanwhile, is on-demand entertainment.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is a hugely anticipated release, and it's poised to bring lapsed gamers back into the fold, but anyone who doesn't already have a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S should prepare themselves for sticker shock. That's because, for a variety of reasons, new consoles today are actually hundreds of dollars more expensive than they were when they launched in 2020.

It has been revealed that take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has frankly acknowledged, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't shaking in his boots about what this means for GTA 6. He thinks GTA 6 will be so good and so compelling that people will buy in no matter what.

Sources indicate that "I don’t think it will slow us down any because, you know, we’re delivering, we believe we’re delivering experiences that people want,” Zelnick said. “However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands.".

In terms of companies, products, people, and services that could benefit from the ripple effects of GTA 6's release, Spiegel remarked music associated with the game could surge in listening activity. This has already happened, as streams of Tom Petty's "Love Is A Long Road" surged after the first trailer for GTA 6 used the song back in 2023. More recently, Cliff Richard's 1976 hit "Devil Woman" indicated up in the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix, helping the song reach more people, including young people who maybe never even knew about the song. Spiegel said social media platforms could benefit from GTA 6's release as well, thanks to fans uploading gameplay clips, livestreams, and other forms of user-generated content inspired by GTA 6. Beyond this, the world of food delivery could see an uptick in activity as people opt to stay in to play GTA 6 (while in-person restaurants and other nightlife venues could take a hit).

"The broader point is that the impact could extend into parts of the economy we don't traditionally associate with gaming," Spiegel said. "For business leaders, the question is whether they're competing with this cultural moment for consumer attention or finding ways to participate in it. That's what makes this launch so much more interesting than simply tracking how many copies are sold.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While the Breaking Bad universe would eventually expand to include dozens of characters, the pilot was actually a tidy affair. At its center was Walter White, whose journey would require an actor of extraordinary depth and nuance. It’s not an exaggeration to say that the success or failure of Breaking Bad would rest primarily on his sagging shoulders.

In a recent development, SHARON BIALY, casting director: I don’t know if Bryan knows this, but when Sherry [Bialy] and I went in to meet with Vince to try to get the job as casting directors—­our “audition”—­we literally stated, “You may think we’re crazy. We hope you don’t fire us before you hire us. But what about Bryan Cranston?” And he said, “By golly, that’s who I want. I worked with him on The X-­ Files.”.

Sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time. We were doing Aaron Sorkin’s newly introduced play [The Farnsworth Invention], and Bryan came in and read. We were blown away. He was so talented on Malcolm in the Middle, obviously, but this was live theater with a lot of language. Anyway, Bryan didn’t get the role, but his audition was incredible. And I never forgot it.

It has been revealed that VINCE GILLIGAN, creator: Bryan was the only guy I was thinking of when I wrote the script. I had written an episode of The X-­ Files called “Drive,” which came out in 1998, and I was lucky enough to hire him to play the bad guy.

We were really struggling to cast this role because we needed a guy who could be really scary, someone who could make us feel like our hero, Agent Mulder, could get his head blown off at any second. But also, he had to be kind of an asshole. [Throughout the episode] he’s ranting about the government. He’s ranting about stuff like, “Agent Mulder— is that a Jewish name?”.

Sources indicate that he’s a thoroughly unlikable guy. And yet you had to feel bad for him, for what happens to him at the end of the episode. You had to feel sympathy.

Recent findings suggest that we only had a day or two left before production was going to start. We were going to have to settle on somebody. We had plenty of actors come in who were scary as all get out, but they weren’t necessarily likable. And then this guy walks in the door: Bryan Cranston. Never heard of him before. And he nails it in the audition. As he left, we all stood up and shook his hand, and then I looked to the other producers and to Rick Millikan, our casting director, and I said, “Off to wardrobe!” He was that good.

When I came up with the idea of Breaking Bad, I thought, This is a guy who, again, is going to be very unlikable. He’s going to do a lot of unlikable things, and the audience still has to sympathize with him. Who would be good for this role? I know! That guy, Bryan Cranston. And I wrote it for him. I never really had anyone else in mind.

MELISSA BERNSTEIN, co-executive producer: He was in an episode of X-­Files, playing this racist, and somehow, over the course of the episode, you go from loathing him to feeling badly that he doesn’t make it. He just was able to make someone so unsavory be human. Vince also said, “And he’s so great with comedy. I just feel it in my bones that he could bring those chops to drama—­his sense of timing, the way he embodies those choices physically. He’s perfect.”.

Sources indicate that BRYAN CRANSTON: I instruct young actors all the time that without a healthy dose of luck, you will not have a career. And this [episode of The X-­ Files] was a lucky break for me.

I had just gotten back from shooting this little movie that I wrote and directed, called Last Chance. I spent all of our money on it, and by the end I was like, Wow, what are we doing on this film? But we rolled the dice on it, and now I was back in town and got a call from my agent about an audition. I said, “Whatever it is, let me know, because I really could use the money.” It just so happened that my look at the time, from this movie that I did, was a perfect look for this guy [on The X-­Files]. So, I went in, and I got the job—­and I was grateful for it.

Sources indicate that it’s only in retrospect that I realized Vince Gilligan wanted to see me [to discuss Breaking Bad] was because I had played this reprehensible character that, despite his actions, still needed the audience to root for his life. Despite the despicable person in the back seat, David Du­chovny’s humanity would not allow him to just pull over and say, “Fuck it, die. You’re a horrible human being. I just want you to die.” He couldn’t do it. That’s really, in a nutshell, what Vince Gilligan does.

I knew intuitively that coming off seven years of a comedy, I needed to look for a drama. If I didn’t, I could have been typecast. If you want to expand on the opportunities that may present themselves, you need to take control. I was offered a couple of comedy pilots that I turned down, and I was perfectly willing to wait. Then Breaking Bad came into my lap.

I read it . . . and I couldn’t believe it. I was stunned. I thought, This is perhaps the best hour­-long screenplay that I’ve ever read. I felt tremendous empathy for this character. This poor guy who is just struggling. And I was the same age as Walter White—­I was fifty.

Sources indicate that but reading the pilot, I didn’t know where it was going. You have this fish­ out­ of­ water teacher, cooking crystal meth? How could that possibly be sustained year after year after year? How can someone who knows nothing about that world survive? And Vince explained that he wanted to turn Mr. Chips into Scarface.

Industry observers note that MARK JOHNSON, executive producer: Obviously, some people came up for Walter White who were names, but we never got around to entertaining them seriously. It was Vince’s idea to cast him. And despite the fact that there wasn’t a unanimous wave of approval, there wasn’t the kind of pushback that you’d probably have today, in large part because I don’t think the expectation was that we were going to get any real name, any big name.

Industry observers note that MELISSA BERNSTEIN: AMC had found Jon Hamm for Mad Men, and they sort of got to reintroduce him to the business. I think they thought we would do something similar with Bryan.

CHARLIE COLLIER, president, general manager, AMC: I was never in the room when they were debating the cast with Vince and Mark. That would have been the programming group. And then they would come back to us and say, “They want that father from Malcolm in the Middle.” And we’d be like, “Really? He’s going to be the linchpin for this whole ambitious project?”.

CHRISTINA WAYNE, senior VP, scripted programming, AMC: When Vince suggested Bryan, we all kind of said, “That guy from Malcolm in the Middle?” And then he started showing us a bunch of tape of Bryan in other things, and I was, like, Oh my God—­he’s a total chameleon.

Industry observers note that JAMIE ERLICHT, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: It’s funny. This is one of those great Hollywood stories that has been told so many times. You sit on the sidelines and watch, and it takes on a life of its own. That life is a little different than the truth, sure, but it’s a better story.

Recent findings suggest that the story is that Zack [Van Amburg] and I heard “Bryan Cranston,” and we were really unsure, and we tried to convince Vince that, No, that’s not the way to go. That’s part of a story about how despite all the forces against him, Bryan Cranston became Walter White.

In a recent development, it’s a great story. I love that story. I mean, I don’t love that story.

According to recent reports, the truth is, the show was going forward. We weren’t worried about the writing because Vince was knocking it out of the park. The directing? We weren’t worried about the directing. The casting was going to be the next critical element. If you don’t have it—­ well, it’s funny to think about it now. With ninety­ nine point nine percent of other actors in that role, that show is just a well­ written good show that doesn’t become the legacy show that it’s become. And so Vince brought up Bryan Cranston.

I had worked with Bryan on King of Queens. He was the wacky neighbor, a guest star. I was a mid­ level executive, and I was in charge of that show. I always thought he brought a lot of comedic value, just like he did on Seinfeld, and obviously Malcolm in the Middle.

So, when the name Bryan Cranston came up, I was like, Hmmm, that’s interesting. I’ve never seen him do the more dramatic stuff. Do you think he can do it?

Vince was very passionate. He stated he had worked with him on X-­Files, and that’s where he really saw what he was capable of on the drama side. We said, “Great, would you send us the X-­Files episode?” Which he did. I remember it was the next day. Zack and I were watching it. We looked at each other and said, “It’s a little bit of a leap of faith, but Vince is passionate, and Bryan is truly talented. Sure, we’re in.” The process took all of thirty­ six hours.

That version of the story, the true version of the story, is not as sexy as the one where Bryan jumped through thirty­ nine hoops and almost didn’t get cast. But that’s how it happened.

According to recent reports, ZACK VAN AMBURG, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: Remember, at this point, Michael Chiklis had gone from doing comedy to being a badass antihero (in The Shield). So, on one hand, you worry: Wait, are we just pulling a page out of the same playbook? Let’s take another sitcom guy and have him do a dark drama.

I think Vince was really clear on why he wanted Bryan. There was a likability factor that was undeniable. There was also a sort of sympathy that Bryan was able to elicit. And Vince also said, “No, wait a second—­ this guy’s also a dramatic actor.”.

While some of this stuff gets lost in the haze of time—­ and the internet has a way of transforming rumors into something disguised as fact—­ it’s fair to say that Bryan was always the first choice for the role of Walter White. Regardless of what you may have heard, no one else was offered the job. Not Matthew Broderick, not John Cusack. No one. But you can’t fault anyone for doing their due diligence.

Sources indicate that SHARON BIALY: The network likes names. They want to talk about other names. We did that. We did a couple of auditions and meetings. We just met recently with an actor on something else, and he reminded me that he was in the waiting room when Bryan walked out, and he turned to the other three actors and said, “We should all just go home. It’s over. That guy’s going to get it.”.

Recent findings suggest that VINCE GILLIGAN: We saw a lot of really good actors, several of them now famous names. They never dissuaded me that Bryan was the guy. And luckily, Bryan mentioned yes, because he was up at the same time for a pilot for Fox that was going to pay him . . . well, my understanding is, substantially more money. Like a doctor show. Thank goodness he went with us instead.

  • Xbox has revealed more details about its next-gen device, Project Helix, describing it as a "console capable of playing games from your PC.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, xbox has revealed more details about its next-gen device, Project Helix, describing it as a "console capable of playing games from your PC." Prominently featured in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, VP of next-gen Jason Ronald said the Xbox Series X|S successor is designed to build on the successes — and hard lessons — of previous Xbox generations, with fewer barriers to play. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine--one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games." Ronald added that the Project Helix family of devices isn't purely focused on traditional next-gen themes like better graphics, but on thinking ahead to create "innovative" experiences. "We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K, or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics--it's really about gameplay innovation," Ronald explained. "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WB0C8z2j6nA Project Helix will also let "hardcore" gamers customize their gaming experience, but how much will all of this cost? Xbox isn't revealing a ballpark figure for Project Helix yet, but Ronald did mention the company is aiming to balance state-of-the-art gaming with an "affordable" price tag. Game preservation will also play a key role, letting users bring their Xbox library with them, and Ronald teased Project Helix as a brand that spans multiple facets of gaming, from living room experiences to handheld sessions and cloud streaming. As a sign of things to come, the Xbox mode on the recently released ROG Xbox Ally was mentioned as the direction the gaming division is headed. The news on Project Helix comes at a time when Xbox has had several highs and lows throughout 2026. This year saw several first-party games release and earn plenty of acclaim, while the anniversary celebrations included a special-edition Xbox Series X that few people could get their hands on — for retail price, that is. At the same time, the rise of Asha Sharma as Xbox CEO has seen scores of jobs and studios slashed from the Xbox family as the company undergoes a "reset" aimed at making it more profitable.

Breaking: 10 Google Privacy Hacks Everyone Should Know

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that from managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it.
  • Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address.
  • Industry observers note that if you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that from managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it. That is a lot of power in the hands of a company that makes money by selling your data to advertisers. While you can't fully escape Google's tracking without quitting a whole bunch of essential online services, you can use these privacy hacks to reduce how the company tracks you, as well as protect the information in your Google account.

Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address. In fact, it has unlimited addresses, but you need a hack to utilize them. When you're signing up for a new service, you can add another word to your email address, as well as the "+" symbol, to create an alias. For example, if your email is "[email protected]," and you're signing up for an Amazon account, you can use "[email protected]" as your email address. The email will still end up in your main inbox, as if you simply used [email protected]. Not only can this trick turn one Gmail address into an unlimited number of addresses, but it also helps you identify who sold your email address to spammers, because those emails will have the alias in the "To" field.

Industry observers note that if you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail. This lets you send and receive emails via your Gmail address, while using Proton Mail's privacy protections such as blocking email trackers.

In a recent development, google wants to show you personalized search results, which initially feels very helpful, but it also ends up trapping you in an algorithmic bubble. The best way to break out of your search bubble is to periodically use other search engines, but if you wish to stick to Google, you can disable personalized search recommendations in Google Search and the Play Store on Android. Go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized Recommendations and Play Personalization.

Google tracks your web and app activity by default, which includes your search history, voice data (if you use the speak-to-search feature), and activity from sites, apps, and devices that use Google services. However, associated information, such as your location data, is also saved to your Google profile, which you might not assume gets included in "Web & app activity." Fortunately, you can disable this tracking by going to this settings page, scrolling down to "Web & App Activity," and turning off all options in this section.

It has been revealed that google's Timeline feature saves your location in Google Maps to create a map of places you've visited. This is useful if you want to keep track of your recent stops; however, Google can use Timeline data to help businesses see how effective their ads were, or how likely you are to visit nearby stores. Its confirmation page confirms this: "Depending on your settings, activity saved as history in your Google Account, including ad interactions, may also be connected to Timeline data to help nearby businesses estimate the likelihood that people will visit their stores. No personal information is shared with businesses.".

Timeline isn't enabled by default, but in case you enabled it a while ago, and are no longer using it, you can turn it off by going to this settings page. Click Turn off, and delete your activity to remove Timeline data from your Google account.

You can't fully escape Google's ads or tracking, but you can disable personalized ads to stop the company from using your account data to show ads. To do this, go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized ads.

Sources indicate that while Google claims that it isn't using your emails to train AI, the company does offer AI features that make your emails feel more robotic than human. One of these is "Smart Reply," which offers email reply suggestions such as "Got it. See you soon." I can type that on my own, and I feel uncomfortable with Gmail analyzing the contents of my emails and replies to offer suggestions that I wouldn't use anyway. You can disable this by going to Gmail Settings > General, or by visiting this settings page. Scroll down to "Smart features," and turn off the checkbox next to it. This will disable Smart Compose, Smart Reply, suggestions for pending replies and follow-ups, spelling, grammar, and autocorrect.

Sources indicate that A physical security key is a great security upgrade. It's a physical barrier that prevents most ways to hack into your account remotely. Even if someone discovers your email ID and password, and has access to your two-factor authentication code, they won't get in without physical access to that key. You can check out Google's support page for physical security keys for more information on compatibility and setting up your security keys.

If you're serious about your online privacy and security, I'd advise against keeping your primary credit card saved to your Google account. If your account is compromised or your device is stolen, you risk exposing your credit card to fraud. Instead, use a prepaid virtual card with your Google account. Sites such as Privacy.com offer single-use or merchant-locked prepaid cards, and they allow you to set spending limits too. You can use such services with your Google account to reduce the chances of losing money if your account gets hacked.

Google uses data from Gmail and Google Drive to target ads, which means that your emails, files, and photos could be used for monetization. To stop this, you'll need to disable Personal Intelligence. To turn it off, visit this settings page, and click Turn off Personal Intelligence.
